answer_sql:
SELECT
  p.brand AS "brand",
  ROUND(SUM(l.gross_amount) - SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS "margin (gross minus net)",
  ROUND(SUM(l.gross_amount), 2) AS "gross",
  ROUND(SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS "net"
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
JOIN contoso_served.dim_product AS p
  ON l.product_key = p.product_key
JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
  ON l.customer_key = c.customer_key
WHERE
  c.continent = 'Europe'
GROUP BY
  p.brand
ORDER BY
  "margin (gross minus net)" DESC
LIMIT 1

body.value: One row, as returned: Adventure Works. Its European sales would have listed for 16,790,109.21 USD and were actually charged out at 15,791,952.49 USD, leaving a gap of 998,156.72 USD — the largest such gap of the eleven brands, 31% ahead of the runner-up Contoso at 759,507.67. WHAT THE CLAIMED FIGURE IS: the money Adventure Works did not collect on its European sales because of discounting. This bundle declares discount_amount to be exactly gross_amount minus net_amount, so the subtraction the question asked for produces the discount given away, not profit earned. Adventure Works' actual profit on those same sales — net revenue minus cost of goods, which is what this bundle calls Margin — is 8,837,878.37 USD, and it leads that ranking as well, so the answer holds under either sense of the word. WHAT IS NOT IN IT: no cost of goods; no sales outside Europe (151,942 of the 223,974 lines are excluded); no narrower period than the full ten years; and no percentage scaling, under which a different brand would win.

value: The 72,032 sales lines (of 223,974) bought by customers whose `dim_customer.continent` is 'Europe', grouped into the 11 brands carried on `dim_product.brand`. Every restriction I applied, and its source: (1) EUROPE AS THE CUSTOMER'S CONTINENT — 'Europe' is a declared value in exactly one column in this bundle, `dim_customer.continent`; `country.default.whose_country_is_asked_never_assumed` (C) forbids choosing between the store and the customer silently and declares no default, so I measured both readings and took this one, because `store.resolution.the_channel_is_the_location_sentinel` records the operator's 2026-10-18 ruling that a measure question spans both channels and a store's country cannot place an online sale (it carries the `--` sentinel). The store-country alternative covers 42,133 lines and gives 625,678.36 for this same winning brand. (2) ALL TEN YEARS — order_date from 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31, per `order.default.an_unscoped_question_covers_all_time` (C), the question having named no period; measured on order_date rather than delivery_date per `order.default.period_is_order_date`. (3) BOTH CHANNELS — shops and web shop together, 29,899 of these lines being online; no channel predicate applied. (4) NO BRAND EXCLUDED — all 11 brands have European sales, so the understanding's 'brands with no European sales are left out' removes nobody. (5) NO MINIMUM-VOLUME QUALIFICATION, which the decomposition flagged as inexpressible; it cannot have affected this answer, since Adventure Works also has the largest European gross of any brand and so no threshold that retains any brand could unseat it.

WITH euro AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    country_code
  FROM contoso_served.dim_customer
  WHERE
    continent = 'Europe'
)
SELECT
  'A: customer lives in Europe' AS reading,
  COUNT(*) AS lines,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.brand) AS brands,
  ROUND(SUM(l.gross_amount), 2) AS gross,
  ROUND(SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS net,
  ROUND(SUM(l.gross_amount - l.net_amount), 2) AS gross_minus_net,
  ROUND(SUM(l.margin_amount), 2) AS margin_amount,
  SUM(CASE WHEN l.channel = 'online' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS online_lines
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
  ON l.customer_key = c.customer_key
JOIN contoso_served.dim_product AS p
  ON l.product_key = p.product_key
WHERE
  c.continent = 'Europe'
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'B: store trades in a European country',
  COUNT(*),
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.brand),
  ROUND(SUM(l.gross_amount), 2),
  ROUND(SUM(l.net_amount), 2),
  ROUND(SUM(l.gross_amount - l.net_amount), 2),
  ROUND(SUM(l.margin_amount), 2),
  SUM(CASE WHEN l.channel = 'online' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
JOIN contoso_served.dim_store AS s
  ON l.store_key = s.store_key
JOIN contoso_served.dim_product AS p
  ON l.product_key = p.product_key
WHERE
  s.country_code IN (
    SELECT
      country_code
    FROM euro
  )
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'C: every line, no Europe filter',
  COUNT(*),
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.brand),
  ROUND(SUM(l.gross_amount), 2),
  ROUND(SUM(l.net_amount), 2),
  ROUND(SUM(l.gross_amount - l.net_amount), 2),
  ROUND(SUM(l.margin_amount), 2),
  SUM(CASE WHEN l.channel = 'online' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
JOIN contoso_served.dim_product AS p
  ON l.product_key = p.product_key
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'D: country codes carrying >1 continent (0 = clean roll-up)',
  COUNT(*),
  NULL,
  NULL,
  NULL,
  NULL,
  NULL,
  NULL
FROM (
  SELECT
    country_code
  FROM contoso_served.dim_customer
  GROUP BY
    country_code
  HAVING
    COUNT(DISTINCT continent) > 1
)

WITH euro AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    country_code
  FROM contoso_served.dim_customer
  WHERE
    continent = 'Europe'
)
SELECT
  p.brand,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN c.continent = 'Europe' THEN l.gross_amount - l.net_amount END), 2) AS a_gross_minus_net,
  ROUND(
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN s.country_code IN (
          SELECT
            country_code
          FROM euro
        )
        THEN l.gross_amount - l.net_amount
      END
    ),
    2
  ) AS b_gross_minus_net,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN c.continent = 'Europe' THEN l.margin_amount END), 2) AS a_declared_margin,
  ROUND(
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN s.country_code IN (
          SELECT
            country_code
          FROM euro
        )
        THEN l.margin_amount
      END
    ),
    2
  ) AS b_declared_margin,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN c.continent = 'Europe' THEN l.gross_amount END), 2) AS a_gross,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN c.continent = 'Europe' THEN l.net_amount END), 2) AS a_net
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
JOIN contoso_served.dim_product AS p
  ON l.product_key = p.product_key
JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
  ON l.customer_key = c.customer_key
JOIN contoso_served.dim_store AS s
  ON l.store_key = s.store_key
GROUP BY
  p.brand

  ROUND(SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS net,

  ROUND(SUM(l.discount_amount), 2) AS declared_discount,
  ROUND(SUM(l.gross_amount) - SUM(l.net_amount) - SUM(l.discount_amount), 2) AS should_be_zero,

The next two columns test what that gap really is: if `should_be_zero` is 0.00 on every row, the figure is identical to this bundle's declared discount, i.e. the money handed back to customers, which is the opposite of profit. The final column is the bundle's own Margin for the same brands and lines — net minus what the goods cost Contoso — which is the figure a reader asking about margin may actually have in mind, and it is roughly nine times larger.

WITH b AS (
  SELECT
    p.brand,
    SUM(l.gross_amount) AS gross,
    SUM(l.net_amount) AS net,
    SUM(l.gross_amount) - SUM(l.net_amount) AS gmn_amount,
    100.0 * (
      SUM(l.gross_amount) - SUM(l.net_amount)
    ) / SUM(l.gross_amount) AS gmn_pct,
    SUM(l.margin_amount) AS m_amount,
    100.0 * SUM(l.margin_amount) / SUM(l.net_amount) AS m_pct
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_product AS p
    ON l.product_key = p.product_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
    ON l.customer_key = c.customer_key
  WHERE
    c.continent = 'Europe'
  GROUP BY
    p.brand
), r AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY gmn_amount DESC) AS rk_gmn_amount,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY gmn_pct DESC) AS rk_gmn_pct,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY m_amount DESC) AS rk_m_amount,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY m_pct DESC) AS rk_m_pct
  FROM b
)
SELECT
  brand,
  ROUND(gmn_amount, 2) AS gmn_amount,
  rk_gmn_amount,
  ROUND(gmn_pct, 4) AS gmn_pct,
  rk_gmn_pct,
  ROUND(m_amount, 2) AS m_amount,
  rk_m_amount,
  ROUND(m_pct, 4) AS m_pct,
  rk_m_pct,
  ROUND(gross, 2) AS gross,
  ROUND(net, 2) AS net
FROM r
WHERE
  rk_gmn_amount = 1 OR rk_gmn_pct = 1 OR rk_m_amount = 1 OR rk_m_pct = 1
ORDER BY
  rk_gmn_amount

value.sql:
SELECT
  p.brand AS "brand",
  ROUND(SUM(l.gross_amount) - SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS "margin (gross minus net)",
  ROUND(SUM(l.gross_amount), 2) AS "gross",
  ROUND(SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS "net"
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
JOIN contoso_served.dim_product AS p
  ON l.product_key = p.product_key
JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
  ON l.customer_key = c.customer_key
WHERE
  c.continent = 'Europe'
GROUP BY
  p.brand
ORDER BY
  "margin (gross minus net)" DESC
LIMIT 1
value.means: One row, as returned: Adventure Works. Its European sales would have listed for 16,790,109.21 USD and were actually charged out at 15,791,952.49 USD, leaving a gap of 998,156.72 USD — the largest such gap of the eleven brands, 31% ahead of the runner-up Contoso at 759,507.67. WHAT THE CLAIMED FIGURE IS: the money Adventure Works did not collect on its European sales because of discounting. This bundle declares discount_amount to be exactly gross_amount minus net_amount, so the subtraction the question asked for produces the discount given away, not profit earned. Adventure Works' actual profit on those same sales — net revenue minus cost of goods, which is what this bundle calls Margin — is 8,837,878.37 USD, and it leads that ranking as well, so the answer holds under either sense of the word. WHAT IS NOT IN IT: no cost of goods; no sales outside Europe (151,942 of the 223,974 lines are excluded); no narrower period than the full ten years; and no percentage scaling, under which a different brand would win.
